Outstanding violations of 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/07/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Bell Township, Westmoreland county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/07/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8270023
Permit API: 129-24699
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Bell Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/07/2026
Comments: On April 7 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the H C McCullough 2 OG Well in regards to CTS 396257. Present during the inspection was Matt Woods (PADEP) and Darren Reilly (PADEP).The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection the well appeared to be equipped for production. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it which contained the well name and API. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges from the wellhead were observed at the surface. A production tank was observed onsite. Affixed to the production tank was a well posting which appeared to contain all required information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H).Upon inspection of the production tank and associated piping, the Department observed what appeared to be a crack in the dump-line leading to the production tank. Under the apparent crack, the Department observed dark oil-like staining on the ground. The Department did not observe any fluid actively leaking from the cracked pipe at the time of the inspection. Conductivity readings of 0.07mS and 0.14mS were obtained in the area of dark staining. These readings appear comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.16mS. While the conductivity readings do not suggest a brine release has occurred, it still appears a release (most likely hydrocarbon/oil based) is occurring/has occurred onsite.Prior to leaving the site, the Department contacted operator representative Heather Empfield via phone call. The Department informed Ms. Empfield of the observed crack in the piping as well as the staining on the ground directly beneath. Ms. Emfield stated field crews would assess the site and remediate any release as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/02/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8164246
Permit API: 081-21912
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/02/2023
Comments: On November 2, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Pad D. Kirby Steck from Range Resources reported a spill of approximately 3.5 barrels of production fluid. The spill occurred when a water hauling truck operator forgot to close a valve on the production fluid tanks after removing the production fluid from the tank causing the production fluid to spill on the well pad surface. The production fluid was spilled on the south corner of the well pad at approximate coordinates 41.4837421, -77.1143370. Range Resources contractors onsite immediately began vacuuming the fluid up off the well pad surface. Range Resources delineated the area of impact and contractors began excavating the area of impact. The excavation area was about eighty feet by thirty feet with a depth of about six inches. The impacted soil was placed on containment and Range Resources is awaiting roll off dumpsters to arrive. The excavation of the area had been completed prior to DEP's arrival onsite. DEP screened the area of the reported spill with a soil conductivity meter and conductivity levels were not found above 500 uS/cm. The DEP observed the discharge area of a nearby sump for the pad and screened the discharge area with a soil conductivity meter. The discharge area did not have a conductivity measurement over 200 uS/cm. DEP spoke with Range Resources Irv Gleason and Kirby Steck. Mr. Steck said Moody and Associates are planning to collect Act 2 confirmatory samples on November 3, 2023. Due to the spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301 have been noted.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activity. Meeting on site today with STL Company Man Tim Fields. Weather at time of inspection is sunny and 80 degrees Fahrenheit.According to Mr. Fields, Precision Drilling Rig #110 has recently completed cementing the surface casing (depth 670') on the 1001H well (API #035-21329). The Blowout preventer is being nippled up and drilling is expected to resume on the intermediate casing later this evening. This is the second of three wells to be drilled and the rig has previously drilled the surface casing on the 1005H well. Two production wells are shut in during current drilling operations. The rig is drilling on water based mud, but the backyard is currently idle. STL submitted a Request for Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG71-A) application on 6/19/22. The Department approved the request on 6/22/22. The intent of the authorization for onsite drill cuttings processing is to remove the solid fraction from the liquid (drilling muds and fluids) so that drilling fluid can be reused concurrently for further drilling. For more information, refer to the Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1400373).During this inspection, conductivity screenings were taken within rig secondary containment, production fluid containment, and GPU containment. Fluid within containment for the 1009H GPU is observed with conductivity reading of 3.8mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming all secondary containment features associated with production equipment. All containment structures are in good repair and are functioning as designed.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: The operator submitted a Notice of Intent and Alternate Method of Plugging to the Department for the Thunder Unit One 1V gas well. Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/05/2023
Comments: I received a text message on April 3rd 2023 from the OGI that was checking on the flaring operation being conducted on the Hill Lease in Brokenstraw twp Warren county operated by Universal Resource Holdings. He said there was a oil spill that appears to have taken place awhile ago coming from a well close to the one being flared. On 04/04/2023, I followed up on the information, Brad Hofert from Universal resource holding was onsite at the time of my inspection. Brad said a valve had frozen and blew out on the number 21 well over winter. The valve was replaced and absorbent pads were used to clean up around the wellhead. I returned to the site on 04/05/2023 to gather photos and take another look at the extent of the spill.Evidence of the crude made it down slope approx 150 feet but stayed inside the tire ruts. More than likely carried by snow melt and rain. Oil soaked leaves and some oxidized crude can be seen in the tire ruts. The estimated release amount is around 5 gallons of crude. I spoke with Brad about getting the oil soaked leaf litter cleaned up and some of the soil next to the well head removed. He agreed and said he would get a crew together and a mini excavator to scrape up the area near the well head. With the estimated volume of this release and the small affected area, this is a non reportable release. The oil covered leaf litter and impacted soil will need to be properly disposed of.

Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from DCNR that a hunter believed that there was a possible brine discharge from this location. The email was forwarded on 11/18/22, and it had been brought to the operator's attention on 11/17.It appears as though a brine leak has occurred sometime between DEP's 4/20/22 inspection and now. It is uncertain which tank the leak is emanating from, as the containment has been compromised and deer tracks are evident throughout.Some volume of brine has leached through the soil and come out on the east side of the containment on the edge of a swale. Significant deer activity has occurred at this point, causing rutting and erosion on the bank of the containment. Conductivity over 1 mS was noted with a meter at several points in the soil. The swale is currently running water, with slightly elevated conductivity noted in the water. As such, it is clear that brine discharge has occurred.The operator was contacted and stated that they would have someone visit the site on 11/30 to inspect, and would begin remediation after. Followup inspection will be done as necessary.

Inspection Date: 10/10/2023
Comments: On 10/10/2023, I conducted an inspection due to an incident that occurred on 10/06/2023. A gathering line inside of the tank battery containment which is located 290 feet to the south from the Arnold #2, had failed and crude oil traveled down slope from the tank battery area, aprox. 90 feet away. A neighbor had complained to the pumper, reporting that they smelled gas on Wednesday October 5th or Thursday October 6th. The pumper had looked around and found nothing on those days. On the evening of Friday October 6th crude was discovered inside and outside the containment. Sam Harvey of Bull Run notified the Department of the release on the Arnold lease owned by Armac Resources on Saturday October 7th.The gathering line ran through the dike wall, it is not clear whether the dike wall failed or if the line leaked outside of containment or both. Crude oil is visible outside of containment. When I arrived on site, the area as seen in the photos was already mulched and seeded. I removed several patches of mulch and smelled the soil underneath he mulch, the soil had a strong distinct smell of crude oil. The southwest side of the dike wall has been excavated and the contaminated material was placed inside of a roll off that remains onsite. It is unclear how much if any soil has been removed in the downslope area below the tank battery.There is no evidence of production fluid in the road ditch located along Bauer Hill road. A boom has been placed in the dry ditch as a precaution. I spoke with Sam Harvey and Justin Hansen of Bull Run (who are contract pumping and facilitating the clean up for Armac Resources). I suggested that an underflow dam be placed at the bottom of the area that has been mulched (base of hill), this is to prevent any remaining production fluid from being washed down to the road side ditch of Bauer Hill which leads to an unnamed tributary of Glade Run.

Comments: On 02/11/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Veres Well Pad in Greene Township, Greene County following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/11/2026 from Greylock. I received a call from Trevor Wood, a representative from Greylock notifying me of the spill. I responded to the incident prior to it being assigned to Oil and Gas in our complaint system. I was accompanied by Keith from Greylock onsite. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/11/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of produced water from a truck was released onto the pad on 02/11/2026. The spill was identified at 8:50 AM and reported to the hotline at approximately 9:43 AM. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1).The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).The spill occurred when a water truck was drawing down produced water from tank. It was believed a pump failed which caused produced water to spray onto the pad, tank and along tank containment. The area impacted was approximately 20ft by 20ft. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 3-6).A conductivity reading was taken in the middle of the impacted area and read 9.09 mS/cm. (Photo 7). Conductivity reading taken in gravel adjacent to separators in front of the tanks was 5.90 mS/cm (Photo 8, 9).I did not observe any spray on the backside of the tanks looking toward the spill area (Photo 10). The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of produced water violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, and 91.34(a).

The Repsol representative stated that the release occurred while a well tender was inside the GPU so the individual was able to stop the release immediately. No puddles, slush, or stains can be observed anywhere on the pad. The excavated hole had snow in it as well. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Inspection Date: 6/02/2026
Comments: On 6/2/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and had just finished the 72HU on 6/1/2026. The crew has completed the stages on the other four wells. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/9/2026.Stimulation operations were being conducted within secondary containment. There were 32 frac tanks stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad, four for freshwater and 28 for produced water. Additionally, there were four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks staged in secondary containment on the pad. Chemical tanks and totes were staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells were stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade, the well pad and associated diversion berms were adequately stabilized. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.During the inspection, I field screened the following for conductivity: A 2' x 3' puddle of water above the center outfall from the north side of the pad, tested at 7.81 mS conductance. Liquid flowing from the center north outfall into the basin tested at 8.08 mS conductance. Liquid in the basin near the northeast outfall tested at 4.04 mS conductance. I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello on location during the inspection. He was collecting water samples from the location. I discussed my findings with him.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and had just finished the 72HU on 6/1/2026. The crew has completed the stages on the other four wells. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/9/2026.Stimulation operations were being conducted within secondary containment. There were 32 frac tanks stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad, four for freshwater and 28 for produced water. Additionally, there were four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks staged in secondary containment on the pad. Chemical tanks and totes were staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells were stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade, the well pad and associated diversion berms were adequately stabilized. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.During the inspection, I field screened the following for conductivity: A 2' x 3' puddle of water above the center outfall from the north side of the pad, tested at 7.81 mS conductance. Liquid flowing from the center north outfall into the basin tested at 8.08 mS conductance. Liquid in the basin near the northeast outfall tested at 4.04 mS conductance. I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello on location during the inspection. He was collecting water samples from the location. I discussed my findings with him.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.
